leads.summary: The new byte-budget test passes on the previous, character-counting implementation
leads.consequence: The 80 options containing 2,000 invalid UTF-8 bytes each become approximately 160,000 replacement Unicode characters. That exceeds the 120,000 limit even if Bash incorrectly counts characters instead of bytes, so the asserted oversize diagnostic and status 1 do not distinguish the old bug from the new fix. The test passes at the head AND with the exact previous-head line options_json_bytes=${#options_json}. A plausible future regression to the character count would go green. Add a UTF-8 case whose encoded JSON has fewer than 120,000 characters but more than 120,000 bytes, and require the guard's diagnostic before the second Perl invocation (80 options x 900 'é' exhibited the distinction). The small-menu stub writes doneFile but no selection, so its expected exit 1 is consistent with the implementation and does not test this boundary.

leads.summary: Following all interior directory symlinks broadens the search past the requested roots, not just symlink starting points
leads.consequence: A Pictures/Videos tree with a nested symlink to another media tree now includes outside/duplicate paths; if the link points to a large or slow tree, find and the complete sort traverse it before the 500-entry/80,000-byte awk cap takes effect. GNU find -H follows the CLI root without following those interior links. #13018 independently implements -H and its test, run on this head, fails because nested.jpg is included. A maintainer must decide whether nested symlink following is intended and reconcile #13018 before combining the PRs, which touch the same hunk. The observed behavior is a new difference from the base, not an assertion that following interior links is never desirable.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus; confirmed (followup-1)

leads.summary: Aliased or repeated media roots produce duplicated menu rows and consume the limited listing slots
leads.consequence: When a symlinked starting point and its actual directory are both in the colon-separated path list (or two symlinks alias the same directory), find -L returns the same file with two path spellings; sort and awk do not deduplicate. Users see duplicate options and two copies consume the 500-row and 80KB limits, potentially hiding distinct recent files. #13197's fixture, run on this pinned head, offered the identical one.webm twice and failed its one-row assertion. #13197's competing changed hunk uses device:inode deduplication, though it has no byte cap, so integrating it needs an intentional choice about deduplication and budget.
leads.triage: behavioural; confirmed by Opus followup-1; published as one sentence in Related PRs paragraph

leads.summary: The related empty-search feedback PR replaces the same pipeline and does not preserve this PR's budgets or symlink handling
leads.consequence: #7320 captures the full sorted find output in files=$(...) before passing it on a here-string and reports an empty search with status 2, which its transcode and RetroArch callers use for notifications. This PR instead streams through find -L/sort/awk to bound rows and returns menu-select's status. The two heads are diverged and a three-way merge conflicts on the entire pipeline, so a straightforward resolution choosing either side loses the other side's semantics: choosing #7320's branch reopens the unbounded option list and does not follow starting symlinks, choosing this one retains the empty search's usage error and misses #7320's status-2 notifications. Integrate both behaviors explicitly before accepting both PRs. No claim is made about a mechanically merged runtime because the merge has conflicts.
leads.triage: factual; verified via read-only gh (coord/) and Opus draft check; #13197 same author, #13018 different author

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5822053960) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5822128472), checked at `073d4985`.

**Verified:** the size check in `omarchy-menu-select` now counts bytes.

The new test does not detect a return to character counting. A separate question about `find -L`, not covered by earlier reviews, is raised below.

| Earlier finding | Status at `073d4985` |
|---|---|
| The new size check counts characters, not bytes, in a UTF-8 locale | **Resolved** |
| Escaped and invalid UTF-8 bytes grow past the limit after awk | **Resolved**: such listings are now rejected with `options payload too large` |
| 500-file cap is not a byte limit | **Resolved**: no tested `omarchy-menu-file` listing reaches `Argument list too long` |
| Code comments overstate the protection | **Resolved** |
| PR description | **Still present, narrower**: it describes only the lister bounds, not the new 120,000-byte cap in the shared `omarchy-menu-select` or the new test |
| Error goes to stderr only (note) | **Still present**: code paths unchanged |
| Lists between 120,001 and about 130,900 JSON bytes now rejected (note) | **Still present, broader**: now also non-ASCII lists passed directly to `omarchy-menu-select` |
| Earlier resolved items (awk byte budget, "500 **or fewer**", symlink test path) | Unchanged; the symlink test passes |

**Verified:** `options_json_bytes=$(LC_ALL=C; printf '%s' "${#options_json}")` equals the byte count in all 16 locale combinations tested (bash 5.3), including `LANG`, `LC_CTYPE` and `LC_ALL` set to UTF-8 locales and `bash --posix`. The parent shell's locale is unchanged. Isolated runs with the real `omarchy-menu-file` and `omarchy-menu-select` and a stub for the shell IPC hop:

```text
listing (entries kept)               JSON bytes  cbb7a789 (C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8)  073d4985 (all three locales)
long CP1251 names (370)                186,481   Argument list too long (126)     options payload too large (1)
ASCII names in a CP1251 folder (388)   180,033   Argument list too long (126)     options payload too large (1)
60 CJK chars + 40 control bytes (298)  140,061   Argument list too long (126)     options payload too large (1)
long valid Cyrillic UTF-8 (272)         80,513   opens                            opens
```

Payloads for ordinary menus (plain lists, stdin input with width and height, icon rows with tabs and CJK text, quotes and backslashes) are identical to `cbb7a789` apart from temporary paths. The author's "fail closed before Perl hits Argument list too long" holds for the second Perl call and the IPC hop. Collections over the cap are now rejected outright, not truncated, so the stderr-only note above still applies to them.

**Optional test improvement:** `menu-select-options-byte-budget-test.sh` also passes at `cbb7a789`. Its 80 options of 2,000 invalid bytes are 160,641 characters after encoding, already over 120,000 when counted as characters. With `b"\xff"*1400` on line 24, the JSON is 112,641 characters and 336,641 bytes: the test then fails at `cbb7a789` (exit 126) and passes at this head. The test still fails at base, so it guards against removing the check entirely.

## `find -L` also follows symlinks inside the roots

`-L` follows every symlink found during the walk, not only symlinked starting points as the comment at [`omarchy-menu-file:47-49`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/073d498544b81209026370f5287031b68f92fcf2/bin/omarchy-menu-file#L47-L49) describes. `find -L` has been used since the PR's first commit. Isolated runs with synthetic folders, comparing this head with a copy using `-H`:

```text
layout inside the roots                      -L (this head)                       -H copy and base
link to an outside folder + outside file     9 entries                            3 entries
Videos/system -> /usr                        27,553 matches, 1.32 s;              not followed, 0.008 s
                                             all 500 entries from /usr
                                             (the fixture's own files were older)
Videos/up -> home folder (loop)              pictures listed twice (11 for 7);    not followed
                                             find reports a loop, exit still 0
```

`sort -rn` reads the whole walk before the awk cap, so the cap limits the entries shown, not the time spent walking. The exit status is unaffected: find's errors go to `/dev/null` and the script returns the menu's status. Omarchy creates `~/Pictures`, `~/Videos` and `~/Games/roms` as real folders, so this needs links created by the user. A linked ROM subfolder is one case where following is arguably wanted.

**Impact:** For users with symlinks inside their media folders, the picker can list unrelated or duplicated files, and a link to a large tree makes every file-picker open walk that tree. This goes beyond #12665, which is about symlinked starting points.

**Suggested change:** Use `find -H`, which follows only the starting points. In the same runs it still listed files under both symlinked roots, which is the #12665 case. If following links inside the roots is intended, stating that in the comment and PR description would make the choice explicit.

**Related PRs:** #13197 (also by this PR's author) and #13018 address #12665 with `find -H`, and #7320 also changes this pipeline. All three conflict with this PR at the same lines. #13197 also removes duplicates by device and inode. In runs of this head, overlapping roots (for example `Videos -> Pictures`) listed each file twice, so 500 entries showed 250 files. `-H` alone does not change that.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up at `073d4985`, compared with `cbb7a789`, the first reviewed commit `f4a067bd` and base. Isolated command-only runs used the real `omarchy-menu-file` and `omarchy-menu-select`, synthetic file names and folders, the `C.UTF-8`, `en_US.UTF-8` and C locales, GNU findutils 4.11.0, and a stub in place of the shell IPC hop. The PR's new test ran by itself against this head, `cbb7a789` and base. Menu rendering, the real IPC transport, the full test suite, network mounts and the locale of real menu and keybinding launches were not tested. Bash versions older than 5.3 were checked by reading the bash source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
